name: compress-gunzip
algorithm: One-shot: inflate a gzip file of 100 MB of text from memory into one output buffer with the std's decompressor (the gzip row's input, tests/bench/idiomatic/gzip/README.md, but the output is decoded whole, not read in 64 KiB chunks), then add every decompressed byte and the length to the checksum; rounds times. Each column makes its buffer (Mk: its arena) once, before the loop.

skip.c: no std gzip in C (zlib is not std)
skip.rust: no std gzip in Rust (flate2 is a crate; no crate stands in)
skip.mk-wrap: the checksum already uses the wrapping operators; the task has no other arithmetic to wrap

no_counts: B24 does not apply: an idiomatic row compares libraries; every decompressor checks the gzip trailer's CRC-32 and length, and the checksum (the sum of the decompressed bytes plus the length) checks the output
notes: One-shot shape on every side (SC-1): the gzip row (tests/bench/idiomatic/gzip) is the streaming task, reading in 64 KiB chunks; this row is not that task. Mk: std.compress.Gunzip into one arena made before the loop and Reset each round; Gunzip sizes its output from the trailer's ISIZE and decodes straight into it. Zig: flate.Decompress in direct mode (an empty window buffer) with streamRemaining into a fixed std.Io.Writer over one buffer of ISIZE + flate.max_window_len bytes, made once; it also decodes straight into the buffer. Go: compress/gzip has no one-shot form, so one gzip.Reader, Reset each round, is read into one buffer of ISIZE + 1 bytes made once; it copies every byte from its window into the buffer, which is the only form Go's std has. Every column sums the whole output after decoding it.

What still differs: Mk's arena returns a chunk of over 512 KiB to the heap at Reset, so its 100 MB output is a fresh heap allocation, zero filled by Arena.Slice, every round; the Go and Zig buffers are reused. That cost is Mk's API, and is counted against Mk.

The streaming row (Mk's Inflater.NewGzip in 64 KiB reads against the gzip row's Go and Zig sources) is not built: std has no Reader over memory or a file (status/std-compress.md, Requests). C and Rust: no std gzip. Bytes per second = 100,000,000 * rounds / median.
Not published: no number here is a measurement.
